report.title: Adjudicate the append-only event log versus erasure-obligation contradiction
report.question: The spec requires append-only event logs and also privacy obligations that may require erasure; which requirement wins, what is the reconciling design, and what does the current implementation do?
report.answer: Append-only wins for historical log bytes: the event log exists to make in-place edits detectable, and a rewrite that blanks a personal field is exactly that edit. Erasure wins for recoverable personal content going forward: personal fields must not be written as plaintext into the log (write-time minimisation), and any residual operational identifier that may later need to become unrecoverable must be crypto-shredded or stored in an erasable side store. Tombstones do not erase; they overlay. Crypto-shredding preserves the hash chain and destroys plaintext-payload audit. No strategy satisfies unmodified historical bytes AND recoverable historical personal payload AND unrecoverable historical personal payload for the same bytes. The current writer (tools/command-center/close.py:append_event) opens EVENTS.jsonl in append mode, serialises the payload with no redaction and no hash chain, and exposes no erase API — a planted synthetic email remains recoverable until the line is rewritten. SUCCESS:ADV-0045

adjudication.recoverable_personal_content: erasure wins by exclusion from the log (minimisation; crypto-shred or externalisation for residual identifiers)
adjudication.crypto_shred: preserves chain; destroys plaintext-payload audit after key deletion
adjudication.historical_plaintext_already_in_log: no per-record reconciliation; residual risk is owner-visible
adjudication.current_implementation: tools/command-center/close.py:85 append-mode JSONL, no redaction, no hash chain, no erase API

impossibility.B: historical personal payload recoverable for content audit
impossibility.residual_risk: Plaintext personal fields already written to an append-only log remain recoverable until the entire log file is destroyed as a unit. Per-subject erasure of those bytes is not possible without rewriting history.
impossibility.owner_visible_impact: A subject-erasure request naming personal data already stored as plaintext in the event log cannot be honoured per record. Keeping append-only leaves the field on disk. Honouring erasure by rewrite breaks the audit prefix. The owner must either accept residual personal data in historical events, or destroy/seal the log as a whole and lose that history. New writes must minimise or crypto-shred.

enumerated_targets.claim: Writing a personal field through the live append-only writer then attempting erasure requires mutating the log or leaving the data in place.
close.append_event stores caller payloads as recoverable plaintext JSONL with no redaction, hash chain, or erase API.
A tombstone append breaks raw replay determinism.
A tombstone reconciles erasure with append-only by removing the personal field from the log.
Crypto-shredding a per-record key breaks hash-chain integrity.
Crypto-shredding breaks audit verification of the historical plaintext payload while leaving the chain verifiable.
Payload externalisation preserves chain integrity; erasing the side store makes the payload unrecoverable and replay of personal content fails.
Write-time minimisation prevents new recoverable PII but cannot erase historical plaintext already in the log.
No executed strategy satisfies unmodified historical bytes and recoverable historical personal payload and unrecoverable historical personal payload for the same bytes.

Append-only wins for historical log bytes; erasure wins for recoverable personal content by excluding it from the log (minimisation plus shred/externalisation). Historical plaintext PII already in the log has no per-record reconciliation.

controls.detail: A second seeded record without the personal field remains findable by its control token, so a miss cannot be blamed on a broken search.
Ciphertext decrypts to the original payload before the per-record key is discarded, so post-shred failure is not a broken cipher.
Unmodified prototype chains verify before any erasure overlay.
The planted email and home path are synthetic and were written only to an isolated tempfile, never to live EVENTS.jsonl.
The no-reconciliation case is executed (leave / mutate / shred) and recorded with residual risk and an owner-visible impact statement.

domain_negative_controls.detail: After a tombstone append, the canary email is still present in log bytes. Treating tombstone as erasure is REFUTED.
Rewriting the personal field in a retained line changes the prefix hash. Mutation is detectable and is not append-only.
After the per-record key is discarded, decryption with a zero key does not recover the plaintext.
Every executed attempt fails at least one of A, B, C.

tombstone.note: A tombstone is another append. Raw replay of prior lines is unchanged and deterministic. Privacy-filtered replay is a different function; it does not remove the original bytes.

crypto_shred.note: Deleting the per-record key leaves the hash chain intact and the ciphertext in place. Plaintext payload verification fails after shred. Audit of structure survives; audit of personal content does not.

externalisation.note: The log stores a pointer and content hash. Erasing the side store makes the payload unrecoverable while the chain still verifies. Replay of personal content fails after erase.

minimisation.note: Stripping personal fields at write time prevents new recoverable PII. It cannot unwrite historical plaintext already in the log.

scope.measurement_surface: Isolated tempfile via close.append_event plus an in-process hash-chained prototype. Live EVENTS.jsonl was not mutated.
